title: Basic Trigonometry – SOH CAH TOA
description: Labelling triangle sides, using sin/cos/tan ratios, angles of elevation and depression, exact values, and bearings.

notes.heading: Labelling Sides and SOH CAH TOA
notes.body: In a right-angled triangle, relative to angle θ: Hypotenuse (H) = opposite right angle, longest side. Opposite (O) = side across from θ. Adjacent (A) = side next to θ (not hypotenuse). Ratios: sin θ = O/H (SOH), cos θ = A/H (CAH), tan θ = O/A (TOA).

notes.heading: Finding Unknown Sides
notes.body: Choose the ratio connecting known and unknown sides. Example: find O when H=10, θ=30°: sin 30° = O/10 → O = 10×0.5 = 5. To find A when O known: A = O÷tan θ. Always use degree mode on calculator.

notes.heading: Finding Unknown Angles
notes.body: Use inverse trig functions. Example: sin θ = 0.6 → θ = sin⁻¹(0.6) ≈ 36.9°. If tan θ = O/A = 7/4 = 1.75 → θ = tan⁻¹(1.75) ≈ 60.3°. Inverse functions: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹ (also arcsin, arccos, arctan).

notes.heading: Exact Values, Elevation, Depression, and Bearings
notes.body: Memorise: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 30° = 1/√3; sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2, tan 45° = 1; sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3. Angle of elevation: upward from horizontal. Angle of depression: downward from horizontal.

notes.heading: 📌 Definition — Pythagoras and Right Triangles
notes.body:
📌 Definition: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse $c$ satisfies $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ where $a$ and $b$ are the two shorter sides.

🔑 Key Concept: Trigonometric ratios only apply to right-angled triangles; always confirm a $90^\circ$ angle before using SOH CAH TOA.

💡 Worked Example: A triangle has shorter sides $6\,\text{cm}$ and $8\,\text{cm}$. Hypotenuse $= \sqrt{6^2+8^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10\,\text{cm}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember: The hypotenuse is always the longest side and is opposite the right angle.

⚠️ Common Mistake: Adding the side lengths ($6+8=14$) instead of using $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

notes.heading: 💡 Worked Example — Angle of Elevation
notes.body:
📌 Definition: The angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal to the line of sight.

🔑 How it works: Draw a right-angled triangle with the horizontal distance as the adjacent side and the vertical height as the opposite side.

💡 Worked Example: An observer stands $30\,\text{m}$ from the base of a tower and looks up at an angle of elevation of $40^\circ$ to the top. Height $h = 30 \tan 40^\circ \approx 30 \times 0.839 \approx 25.2\,\text{m}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember: $\tan \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$ is usually the best ratio for elevation and depression problems.

⚠️ Common Mistake: Using the angle with the wrong side or putting opposite/adjacent in the wrong order.

notes.heading: ⚠️ Common Mistakes and ✅ Final Check
notes.body:
📌 Definition: A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, usually written as a three-digit number (e.g. $060^\circ$).

🔑 Key Concept: For bearings, draw a north line at each point and use alternate or co-interior angles where parallel north lines meet a transversal.

💡 Worked Example: A ship sails $5\,\text{km}$ east from port on bearing $090^\circ$, then $5\,\text{km}$ north. The return bearing is $225^\circ$ (south-west), because $\tan \theta = \frac{5}{5}=1$ gives $\theta = 45^\circ$ measured from south.

📎 Key Points to Remember: Check your calculator is in degree mode; label opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse before choosing a ratio.

⚠️ Common Mistake: Confusing the angle of depression with the angle inside the triangle — the angle of depression from the horizontal equals the angle of elevation from below (alternate angles).

✅ Check: Re-read the question, confirm your answer matches what was asked, and round to the required number of significant figures.

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, which side is always opposite the right angle?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle, longest side.

Which ratio to find hypotenuse when angle and adjacent are given?
questions.explanation: CAH: cos θ = A/H → H = A/cos θ.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides $5\,\text{cm}$ and $12\,\text{cm}$. What is the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Pythagoras' theorem states that in a right-angled triangle, $c^2=a^2+b^2$ where $c$ is the hypotenuse. With shorter sides $5\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$, the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{25+144}=\sqrt{169}=13\text{ cm}$. This $5$-$12$-$13$ triangle is a common Pythagorean triple used in construction and navigation.

questions.stem: A ladder leans against a wall, reaching $8\,\text{m}$ up when its base is $6\,\text{m}$ from the wall. How long is the ladder?
From the top of a $30\,\text{m}$ cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is $25^\circ$. What is the horizontal distance to the boat? ($\tan 25^\circ \approx 0.466$)
questions.explanation: Angle of depression equals the angle of elevation, so $\tan 25^\circ = \frac{30}{d}$, giving $d = \frac{30}{\tan 25^\circ} \approx 64.4\,\text{m}$.
Draw a right triangle with adjacent $4$ and hypotenuse $5$; the opposite side is $\sqrt{5^2-4^2}=3$, so $\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}$.

questions.stem: A bearing of $225^\circ$ means the direction is:
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north; $180^\circ$ is south and $270^\circ$ is west, so $225^\circ$ points south-west.
